summary: The LLM landscape in late 2026 is dominated by three major commercial families — OpenAI's GPT, Anthropic's Claude, and Google's Gemini — with open-weight models from Meta, DeepSeek, Mistral, and Alibaba's Qwen providing strong alternatives for self-hosting and cost-sensitive workloads. Enterprise adoption is increasingly mediated through cloud aggregators like AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI, and IBM watsonx, which significantly amplifies the real-world reach of models beyond their direct-API footprint. Pricing continues to fall sharply, with open models closing much of the quality gap against frontier commercial offerings.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.popularity_notes: Consistently the most-called model via OpenAI's API and Azure OpenAI, with the broadest aggregator reach across Azure and third-party platforms, making it the default enterprise and developer choice.
models.best_for: General-purpose production applications requiring multimodal input and reliable tooling.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.popularity_notes: Released Feb 17, 2026, matching Opus-level performance at Sonnet pricing; heavily adopted for coding and available across AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and direct API, driving strong enterprise usage.
strengths: Available on Bedrock and Vertex AI
models.best_for: Software development, agentic coding assistants, and complex reasoning at scale.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.popularity_notes: Extremely high adoption for its combination of very low cost and large context window, distributed broadly through Google Vertex AI and consumer products to drive massive call volume.
models.best_for: High-volume, cost-sensitive tasks needing large context such as document processing.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Google's flagship reasoning model widely used via Vertex AI and the Gemini API, with strong enterprise reach through Google Cloud's aggregator ecosystem.
models.best_for: Complex reasoning and analysis over very large contexts in enterprise settings.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.popularity_notes: Anthropic's fast, low-cost model with growing adoption for high-throughput tasks; benefits from availability on AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI alongside the direct API.
models.best_for: High-volume, latency-sensitive production workloads needing solid quality.

models.name: DeepSeek V3
models.popularity_notes: One of the most-downloaded open-weight models on HuggingFace, offering near-frontier performance at a fraction of commercial costs, driving heavy self-hosted and API adoption.
models.best_for: Cost-sensitive deployments and self-hosting where open weights are required.

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.popularity_notes: Among the most downloaded open models on HuggingFace and widely available across AWS Bedrock, Azure, and Vertex AI, making it a default open-weight choice for enterprises.
models.best_for: Self-hosted and fine-tuned deployments needing a proven open model.

models.name: DeepSeek R1
models.popularity_notes: A hugely popular open-weight reasoning model with massive HuggingFace download volume, widely adopted for low-cost chain-of-thought reasoning.
models.best_for: Reasoning-heavy tasks where open weights and low cost matter.

models.name: Mistral Large 2
models.popularity_notes: Mistral's flagship with strong European enterprise adoption and availability through AWS Bedrock, Azure, and Vertex AI, broadening its real-world reach.
models.best_for: Multilingual and European enterprise deployments with sovereignty needs.

models.name: Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.popularity_notes: A top-downloaded open-weight MoE model on HuggingFace with rapidly growing global adoption, especially strong in Asia and among open-model self-hosters.
models.best_for: Open-weight self-hosting and multilingual applications at scale.
